records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] police responded to the listed location for report of a motor vehicle vs pedestrian crash. i arrived on scene and safd/ems was treating u2 who was laying on the [roadway] [roadway]. u2 was pronounced deceased by md2 winkler at 1949 hours. i notified sapd traffic investigations/tid and sgt price. cover officers shut down all traffic north and southbound on bandera securing the scene. i requested sapd crime scene investigator who arrived to process the scene. u1 had stopped and all occupants were out of vehicle. no injuries reported to me. u1 operator said he was [roadway] [roadway]. u1 operator said he did not see u2 until a split second before impact. u1 operator thought he saw u2 walking/facing westbound. u1 operator said he could not avoid u2 and struck him with the vehicle and then stopped right away. u1 said an unknown black truck ran over u2 but did not stop and left the scene right away. u1 front passenger said she saw u2 right before impact and she thought u2 was [roadway] facing southbound. u1 rear passengers said they did not see u2 until right before impact and they thought u2 was standing [roadway] facing southbound. i spoke with w1 who's information is on the key card. w1 said he was in traffic in his vehicle behind u1. w1 initially told me he did not see what happened. when i asked w1 to confirm if he witnessed this crash w1 said he did. w1 said he saw u1 strike [roadway] [roadway]. w1 said he stopped in front of u2 to stop traffic from running over u2. u1 occupants said it [roadway] from east to west. there was no crosswalk where u2 was. u2 failed to yield the right of way to oncoming traffic. tid arrived to process the scene and speak with u1 occupants and w1. medical examiner spears was informed of this and arrived to process the scene. medical examiner/contract took custody of u2 when scene was finished being processed. u1 was towed by contract wrecker to growdon. u1 operator was given listed citation and [case id] for this crash. body cam/coban available/eor/// #72 **this report was supplemented on [date] by det. p. davis #2406 to add the toxicology results for unit 2 and to update the contributing factors for unit 2.**

records.deidentified_narrative: unit #1 was traveling north west on fm 1686. unit #2 was walking north west along the east edge of the roadway, ahead of unit #1. at approximately 0. 36 miles [roadway], unit #1 struck unit #2. unit #2 was thrown into the ditch on the east side of the roadway. unit #1 was in violation of trc 552. 008, which requires drivers to exercise due care to avoid colliding with a pedestrian on a roadway. unit #2 was walking on the right side of the roadway with the flow of traffic, in violation of trc 552. 006 which requires pedestrians to walk along the left side of the roadway facing oncoming traffic when a sidewalk is not provided. a witness was walking with unit #2 but a little bit ahead of him when a pickup truck heading north west drove past her, she turned around and saw that unit #2 had been struck. the witness said the truck was a light color and she believed it was a flatbed. she also said the vehicle never stopped and continued traveling in the same direction on fm 1686. because the driver of unit #1 failed to stop and render aid as required by trc 550. 021, this will be an ongoing investigation of hit and run. several tips were received in the weeks following this crash regarding possible suspect vehicles. follow up investigation on those tips found no connection between any of those vehicles and this crash. the investigation remains open.

records.public_safe_text: unit #1 was traveling north west on fm 1686. unit #2 was walking north west along the east edge of the roadway, ahead of unit #1. at approximately 0. 36 miles [roadway], unit #1 struck unit #2. unit #2 was thrown into the ditch on the east side of the roadway. unit #1 was in violation of trc 552. 008, which requires drivers to exercise due care to avoid colliding with a pedestrian on a roadway. unit #2 was walking on the right side of the roadway with the flow of traffic, in violation of trc 552. 006 which requires pedestrians to walk along the left side of the roadway facing oncoming traffic when a sidewalk is not provided. a witness was walking with unit #2 but a little bit ahead of him when a pickup truck heading north west drove past her, she turned around and saw that unit #2 had been struck. the witness said the truck was a light color and she believed it was a flatbed. she also said the vehicle never stopped and continued traveling in the same direction on fm 1686. because the driver of unit #1 failed to stop and render aid as required by trc 550. 021, this will be an ongoing investigation of hit and run. several tips were received in the weeks following this crash regarding possible suspect vehicles. follow up investigation on those tips found no connection between any of those vehicles and this crash. the investigation remains open.

records.deidentified_narrative: the scene of this collision was the parking lot of the 'walmart' located at 255 fm 518 in kemah tx. the parking lot is a large, flat, asphalt , parking lot. the p. o. i. was located . 1 miles e. of the [roadway] and approx 18' n. of the front doors of the 'walmart. a painted crosswalk is located at the p. o. i. for use by pedestrians. unit-1 ( schneck) was driving his vehicle s/b through the parking lot of the 'walmart' parking lot. unit-1 turned e/b approx 18-20' n. of the 'walmart' front doors and drove e/b through the crosswalk without stopping. unit-1 failed to yield to (2) pedestrians who were already in this crosswalk, walking n/b from the 'walmart' ( unit-2 triana) and unit-3 ( johnson). unit -1 struck both johnson and triana. johnson suffered injuries to his upper torso. triana was run over by unit-1 and suffered major injuries to her entire body. i was already on scene when the collision occurred but did not witness the incident. i found triana underneath unit-1 bleeding from injuries to her face. the force of the impact knocked triana out of her shoes. upon interviewing unit-1 i learned he has parkinson's and diabetes and takes medication for both medical conditions. unit-1 never saw unit-2 or unit 3 prior to the collision and agreed it may be best to stop driving at this time due to his age and medical condition. this collision was witnessed by james dobbins, wma, dl# 05703328, who had a clear unobstructed view from 100' feet east of the collision. i also collected video surveillance from the 'walmart' which verified my findings in this investigation. cpl. t. powell of galveston county s. o. arrived at the scene and documented the scene and damage to unit-1 with photographs, gcso [case id]. all photos and video submitted to evidence under this [case id] at k. p,d. i am requesting that the d. p. s. reevaluate unit-1's license due to the facts surrounding this collision. this collision occurred on private property and there is no transportation code violations to be cited for

located . 1 miles e. of the [roadway] and approx 18' n. of the front doors of the 'walmart. a painted crosswalk is located at the p. o. i. for use by pedestrians. unit-1 ( schneck) was driving his vehicle s/b through the parking lot of the 'walmart' parking lot. unit-1 turned e/b approx 18-20' n. of the 'walmart' front doors and drove e/b through the crosswalk without stopping. unit-1 failed to yield to (2) pedestrians who were already in this crosswalk, walking n/b from the 'walmart' ( unit-2 triana) and unit-3 ( johnson). unit -1 struck both johnson and triana. johnson suffered injuries to his upper torso. triana was run over by unit-1 and suffered major injuries to her entire body. i was already on scene when the collision occurred but did not witness the incident. i found triana underneath unit-1 bleeding from injuries to her face. the force of the impact knocked triana out of her shoes. upon interviewing unit-1 i learned he has parkinson's and diabetes and takes medication for both medical conditions. unit-1 never saw unit-2 or unit 3 prior to the collision and agreed it may be best to stop driving at this time due to his age and medical condition. this collision was witnessed by james dobbins, wma, dl# 05703328, who had a clear unobstructed view from 100' feet east of the collision. i also collected video surveillance from the 'walmart' which verified my findings in this investigation. cpl. t. powell of galveston county s. o. arrived at the scene and documented the scene and damage to unit-1 with photographs, gcso [case id]. all photos and video submitted to evidence under this [case id] at k. p,d. i am requesting that the d. p. s. reevaluate unit-1's license due to the facts surrounding this collision. this collision occurred on private property and there is no transportation code violations to be cited for
